title: Conditional PED-ANOVA: Hyperparameter Importance in Hierarchical & Dynamic Search Spaces

problem.claim: Hyperparameter importance must be estimated in conditional search spaces where a hyperparameter's presence or domain can depend on other hyperparameters.

gap.claim: Original PED-ANOVA assumes a fixed, unconditional search space and cannot properly handle conditional hyperparameters.

contributions.claim: Introduces condPED-ANOVA, a framework for estimating hyperparameter importance in conditional search spaces.
Defines conditional hyperparameter importance for top-performing regions and derives a closed-form estimator that accounts for conditional activation and domain changes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments reportedly show that naive adaptations of existing hyperparameter-importance estimators produce misleading or uninterpretable importances in conditional settings.
Experiments reportedly show that condPED-ANOVA consistently produces meaningful importances reflecting the underlying conditional structure.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work targets hyperparameter-importance estimation in conditional search spaces.
Existing PED-ANOVA is limited by its assumption of a fixed, unconditional search space.
The authors introduce conditional importance and a closed-form estimator for conditional activation and domain changes.
Experiments compare naive adaptations with condPED-ANOVA and report more meaningful importances from the proposed method.

source_observation.claim: Naive adaptations of unconditional hyperparameter-importance estimators reportedly become misleading or uninterpretable when hyperparameter activation and domains are conditional.

interpretation.claim: Importance analyses should model conditional structure explicitly rather than applying unconditional estimators without adjustment.

application.claim: Use a conditional importance estimator when analyzing hierarchical or dynamically changing search spaces.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach applies beyond the reported experimental settings.

unknowns: Experimental datasets, search spaces, and evaluation metrics are unspecified.
The abstract does not report quantitative results or comparative performance values.
Theoretical guarantees and estimator assumptions are unspecified.
